meta.strategicSummary: Day 27 of Hormuz closure sees a sharp U.S. military escalation signal: the Pentagon is actively planning ground troop deployments of up to 10,000 and has drawn up target seizure scenarios inside Iran. This is a qualitative step beyond carrier strike group presence — it signals Trump is seriously entertaining kinetic regime-pressure operations, not merely naval deterrence. Credibility jumps materially. The U.S. guarantee (Ps) recovers modestly as allies observe genuine military commitment. However, no ceasefire, diplomatic outreach, or sanctions relief has emerged, meaning Iran's incentive structure (G, S, Sr) is unchanged — the dollar-trap remains fully active. At $100.73 Brent on day 27, markets are pricing sustained disruption but not yet a ground war premium; that changes if troop orders are actually cut.
meta.mostSignificantEvent: Pentagon drawing up scenarios to seize targets within Iran — this crosses from deterrence posturing into actual contingency planning for offensive ground operations, fundamentally altering the escalation ladder and Iran's calculus about whether U.S. threats are bluffs.

headlines.title: The Pentagon is considering 'sending up to 10,000 additional ground troops to the Middle East' to give Trump 'more military options', according to Wall Street Journal report.
Pentagon has 'drawn up scenarios for deploying troops to seize various targets within Iran', according to CNN report.
